Ninth, not accepting instruction from the noble and holy ones;
tenth, despising those of low birth.
Through these ten karmas, one obtains rebirth in a high-born family as the retribution.
The opposite of the preceding cases is as follows:
ten types of karma cause one to obtain a rebirth with meager material resources.
First, one personally commits theft.
Second, inciting others to steal;
third, praising the theft of others;
fourth, feeling joy upon seeing others steal.
Fifth, they diminish the livelihoods of their parents.
Sixth, they seize the resources and wealth of the noble and holy ones.
Seventh, they feel no joy in their hearts when seeing others obtain benefit.
Eighth, creating obstacles to prevent others from obtaining benefit;
ninth, lacking a mind of sympathetic joy when seeing others practice giving;
tenth, feeling no compassion upon seeing famine and instead giving rise to delight.
The ten karmas that cause one to be born with abundant wealth are the reverse of the preceding [ten] and may be understood accordingly.
Regarding the ten gates of merit from worshipping stupas, the subsequent text extensively distinguishes the retributions for various miscellaneous karmas.
By making offerings to Buddha stūpas and temples, one attains ten kinds of merit.
First, one obtains an exquisite complexion and a beautiful voice.
Second, whatever words one utters...
All people believe in and submit to him;
he is fearless in the assemblies of the three realms;
and he is cherished and protected by devas and humans.
Fifth, they possess majestic power;
sixth, sentient beings all come to rely upon them because of their majestic power;
seventh, they constantly attain proximity to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Eighth, one possesses great merit and reward;
ninth, at the end of life, one is reborn in heaven;
tenth, one swiftly realizes nirvana.
The Ten Meritorious Gates of Offering a Canopy: By offering a precious canopy, one attains ten merits.
First, one dwells in the world like a canopy, providing protection and shelter for sentient beings.
Second, his body and mind are stable and at ease, free from all feverish afflictions;
third, he is revered by all, with none daring to treat him with contempt;
fourth, he possesses great majestic power.
Fifth, they shall always be able to draw near to Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of great majestic virtue,
taking them as their retinue.
Sixth, they shall constantly become universal monarchs (cakravartin).
Seventh, one constantly acts as a leader in cultivating wholesome deeds.
The [fruits of the] eight, nine, and ten rewards are like the three [sections] following the worship of the Buddha.

Regarding the ten gates of merit for offering banners: by respectfully offering silk banners, one obtains ten merits. These are the ten gates of merit for offering banners. By respectfully offering silk banners, one obtains ten merits.
First, while dwelling in the world, one is honored, respected, and provided for by kings, ministers, relatives, friends, and spiritual teachers as if one were a banner.
Second, one possesses great wealth and power, endowed with vast riches and treasures.
Third, one's good reputation will spread and reach all directions.
Fourth, one's physical appearance will be dignified and one's lifespan will be long.
Fifth, one will always practice with firm resolve in whatever place of birth one takes.
Sixth, they possess great renown;
seventh, they possess great majestic power;
eighth, they are born into high-ranking families.
Ninth, one will be reborn in the heavens at the end of life.
Tenth, one will swiftly attain nirvana.
Regarding the ten gates of merit from giving bells: by giving bells and chimes, one obtains ten merits.
First, one obtains the Brahma-voice;
second, one possesses great renown; third, one knows past lives;
fourth, all who hear what one says revere and love them.
Fifth, they are always adorned with precious canopies.
Sixth, they wear exquisite necklaces as ornaments.
Seventh, their countenances are upright and dignified, bringing joy to all who behold them.
The remaining three [sections] are as in the three sections following the "Worshiping the Buddha.
Regarding the ten gates of merit for giving robes: by offering garments, one obtains ten merits.
First, one’s face and eyes become dignified and handsome.
Second, their skin is fine and smooth.
Third, dust and grime do not adhere to them.
Fourth, at birth, they are already endowed with exquisite garments.
Fifth, five exquisite bedding materials cover his body.
Sixth, he is clothed in the garments of shame and modesty.
Seventh, all who see him feel reverence and affection.
The remaining three cases follow the same principle as before.
Regarding the gift of vessels and food and drink, one attains ten doors of merit; that is, for both vessels and food and drink, one attains ten merits for each.
As explained in the *Ullambana Sūtra Commentary*, it would be too prolix to describe them in detail here.
Regarding the ten gates of merit from the offering of incense: by respectfully offering incense and flowers, one obtains ten merits.
First, dwelling in the world like a flower;
second, the body is free from foul odors;
third, the fragrance of merit and the fragrance of precepts pervade all directions.
Fourth, the olfactory faculty remains unimpaired in whatever place one is born.
Fifth, one transcends the world to serve as a refuge for all beings.
Sixth, the body is always fragrant and pure.
Seventh, delighting in the true Dharma,
receiving and turning the wheel of the true Dharma,
and receiving, upholding, praising, and reciting it.
The remaining three [sections] are as before.
Regarding the ten gates of merit from the gift of lamps: by giving the light of a lamp, one obtains ten merits.
First, one illuminates the world like a lamp.
Second, the physical eye is not impaired in whatever place one is born.
Third, one attains the divine eye.
Fourth, one attains excellent wisdom regarding wholesome and unwholesome phenomena. Fifth, one eliminates and extinguishes the great darkness.
Sixth, one attains the clarity of wisdom.
Seventh, while transmigrating through the world, one never remains in places of darkness.
The remaining three are as previously described.
The Ten Meritorious Benefits of Respectful Joining of the Palms. Through respectful joining of the palms, one obtains ten meritorious benefits.
First, one obtains superior karmic retribution.
Second, one is born into a noble family;
third, one obtains excellent and wondrous physical form;
fourth, one obtains excellent and wondrous voice.
Fifth, they attain the supreme and wondrous canopy;
sixth, they attain the supreme and wondrous eloquence;
seventh, they attain the supreme and wondrous faith.
Eighth, one attains supreme and wondrous ethical discipline;
ninth, one attains supreme and wondrous extensive learning;
tenth, one attains supreme and wondrous wisdom.
The End of Volume Two of the *Exhortation to Generate the Bodhicitta*.
Originally, this book is the essential path for generating the mind and practicing cultivation;
it is the great foundation for awakening (*bodhi*) and nirvana (*nirvāṇa*).
Those who seek to become Buddhas must not fail to revere [this practice].
According to precedents from previous years,
the household of Seiryōkō-in possesses an imperial vow that has been authorized for the opening of the first volume.
Subsequently, the bhikṣu Jìngzhào of Kōmyō-ji Temple in Kantō specifically made a vow and exhorted others to raise several tens of thousands of coins as pure wealth,
thereby fully preparing the funds for the carving of the middle and lower volumes.
May fellow Dharma-practicing bhikṣus illuminate wisdom, exert themselves in diligent effort, and inspire the worthy through their skillful means.
It is hoped that this shall circulate for all generations,
awakening those of great resolve.
Recorded by the Shamon Eison of Saidai-ji Temple.
